metadata.title: HeirSearch | Consanguinity Chart Walk-Through
metadata.author: HeirSearch
metadata.shortDescription:
According to the ABA, approximately 60% of Americans die without a will. This means that many legal professionals administering estates may have to probate an intestacy.

Who inherits the estate of an intestate person is determined by consanguinity and can vary based on each state’s descent and distribution laws.

One helpful tool for this purpose is our Consanguinity Chart.

In this video, HeirSearch walks legal professionals through our process of harnessing consanguinity to satisfy the courts.

did you know that approximately 68 of
americans die without a will
this means that many legal professionals
administrating estates may have to
probate an intestacy
who inherits the estate of an intestate
person is determined by consanguinity
and can vary based on each state's
dissent and distribution laws
usually in estates recipients are in
order spouse
issue
parents siblings nieces and nephews
and the next of kin including adopted
and half-blood relatives
if the intestate person died with none
of the listed relatives surviving them
we must determine the decedent's lawful
heirs
one helpful tool for this purpose is our
consanguinity chart
this chart outlines the relation between
a decedent and their family members
each box on the chart has a generational
title and a number representing the
degrees of consanguinity or relationship
to begin reading the chart place the
decedent let's call him john smith in
the blank box
the first step is determining if john
has a living spouse and lineal
descendants
this is established by following the
line directly below him to identify his
children grandchildren and
great-grandchildren
if john smith has no living spouse or
lineal descendants
we move on to the next level of the
chart
we call this a level one search as it
begins with his parents who are one
degree of consanguinity away
by identifying the decedent's parents we
verify that we have the correct family
unit
and confirm the number of children
within the family
we then move down the chart to identify
his brothers and sisters nephews and
nieces and if necessary his grand or
great grand nephews and nieces until we
identify living heirs
if john has no siblings and no living
level one heirs we continue to the next
level of the chart
we call this a level two search
as it begins with his grandparents who
are two degrees of consanguinity away
his aunts uncles and first cousins on
both the paternal and maternal sides of
the family are included in this search
as well as his first cousins one time
two times or three times removed when
state law requires
the higher we go up the consanguinity
chart the further back we go into the
decedent's genealogy and the more
complex the family tree becomes
each level up the chart requires that
the previous level of search has proven
there are no living errors
we hope you found this walkthrough of
our consanguinity chart helpful
no matter how complex your probate case
seems airsearch has the genealogical
expertise you need to satisfy the court
with fees quoted in advance and
determined by a set fee schedule based
on the type of search and never as a
percentage
we're ready to help you identify unknown
or missing heirs and beneficiaries
a better way
[Music]
